 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE TUSHAR RAO GEDELA  ORDER % 18.10.2023 [The proceeding has been conducted through Hybrid mode] CRL.M.(BAIL)1470/2023 (for interim suspension of sentence for four weeks)

1. This is an application under Section 389 Cr.P.C., 1973 seeking interim suspension of sentence of the appellant in FIR No. 376/2016 under Sections 376/506 IPC, 1860 read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012 registered with PS-Ranjeet Nagar, Delhi, for a period of four weeks on the ground of unfortunate demise of the brother of the applicant.
2. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that the appellant was convicted on 24.05.2022 and has been directed to This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/10/2023 at 00:02:47 undergo a sentence of 14 years.
According to the Nominal Roll dated 04.02.2023, the appellant has completed 2 years 7 months and 17 days by that time.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the brother of the appellant had unfortunately expired on 07.10.2023 and he got the news on 08.10.2023.
Thereafter, the application was drafted by the jail visiting counsel who took some time to draft the application before the same could be filed before this Court.

1 4. Be that as it may, according to the interim bail application, the appellant wants to attend the last rites of his brother, which were to be held on 17.10.2023 and 27.10.2023 at Village: Bhasor, Gram- Radiyam Bhasor, PS-Baheda, Bhaya Nehda, Anchal BeniPur, Zila:
Darbhanga, Bihar-847233.
5.
So far as the ritual to be conducted on 17.10.2023 is concerned, since the date has gone by, no orders can be passed thereon.

6. So far as the request for 27.10.2023 is concerned, since the State will require some time to confirm the submissions made above, as also to verify the address of the native village of the appellant in Bihar, it may not be possible to pass orders so early in time.

7. The same cannot be also done for the reason that the impending vacations are to commence from 21.10.2023, it may not be possible for the State to verify the aforesaid directions within such a short time period.

8. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits on instructions that apparently there are certain other functions/ rituals, which may be held subsequent to 27.10.2023 and further submits that This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/10/2023 at 00:02:47 the Police may be directed to verify the aforesaid antecedents.
9. Issue notice.

Notice is accepted by Mr. Mukesh Kumar, learned APP for the State, who seeks and is granted 10 days time to verify the aforesaid facts and status report n that regard be placed on record.
10.
An advance copy of the same be furnished to learned counsel for the appellant.
11. In the meanwhile, the updated Nominal Roll be also requisitioned from the concerned Jail Superintendent before the next date of hearing.

In compliance of the mandate of the Supreme Court in Jagjeet Singh & Ors. vs. Ashish Mishra @
Monu & Anr., reported as (2022) 9 SCC 321, let intimation be sent by the Investigating Officer to the complainant, informing her that she is entitled to be heard in the matter, for which she may either remain present or be represented on the next date.
